_about: Access policy as facts (roadmap Epic E). A PolicyRule permits or forbids one Permission for the roles and teams it names; a Permission is an action on a kind of resource, narrowed by a selector over the resource's attributes; a rule may single out the resources it covers. A table or a column says how it is classified and whether it holds personal data, so a selector can say `pii=false`. A Principal is an identity that holds a session, a person's account or a service's, and holds roles; an Agent (the agent pack's) is granted roles of its own, and what it may do for a principal is the intersection of the two (`oto policy snapshot`). Only an active rule compiles (`oto policy compile`, ADR-0004); a rule is a draft until a named person activates it. The generated system runs as principals: a Component runs_as a service account, a Permission names the platform role it maps to (cloud_role), a resource says where it is on the platform (resource_uri), and `oto policy iam` derives the platform's bindings and writes them back as generated Controls that derive from the rules (ADR-0005): a design-time output OTO never enforces. A relation is {domain, range, inverse, definition}. Use A|B for a union.
_summary: Access policy as facts on the data layer: rules that permit or forbid a permission for a role or a team, permissions as an action on a kind of resource narrowed by a selector, classification and personal data on tables and columns, and the active rules compiled into a Cedar bundle. A principal holds roles, an agent is granted some, and the snapshot an agent runs under is the intersection. The generated system's IAM: components running as principals, permissions mapped to platform roles, resources placed on the platform, and the bindings derived from the rules as generated controls, a design-time output.
name: Policy

PolicyRule.definition: One rule of the access policy: it permits or forbids one permission for the roles and teams it names, on every resource the permission's selector admits or only on the resources it singles out. A draft until a named person activates it; a retired one stays as history. Active rules compile into the policy bundle, most urgent (highest priority) first; a forbid outranks a permit.
PolicyRule.scope_note: A kind of the estate's Policy, so what governs it (a Decision) and what documents it are the estate's own relations. Why the rule exists is its rationale; what it says is its effect, permission, roles and resources.

Permission.definition: An action on a kind of resource: read, write, export, delete or admin, on a class of the vocabulary (Table, Column, DataStore, Component, Interface), narrowed by a selector over the resource's attributes (`pii=false`, `classification!=restricted`). A permission is what rules grant or refuse; it holds no roles itself.

Principal.definition: An identity that holds a session: a person's account or a service account, the one on whose behalf an agent acts. It holds roles; what it may do is what the active rules say about those roles, and what an agent may do for it is the intersection of the agent's own grants with its.
Principal.scope_note: Not a Person of the work pack and not a Role: a person has one or more accounts, and an account holds roles. A service account is a principal with no person behind it.

for_role.definition: The roles and teams the rule speaks about. A rule names at least one; in the bundle, each becomes the principal of one policy.

of_permission.definition: The one permission the rule permits or forbids.

singles_out.definition: The resources the rule singles out. Without any, the rule covers every resource of the permission's class that its selector admits.

holds_role.definition: The roles and teams the principal holds, as the identity provider or the organisation says. A principal holds at least one; with none it may do nothing.

granted_role.definition: The roles an agent may exercise on its own account, granted by whoever owns it. What it actually does for a principal is bounded by the principal's roles too: the snapshot is the intersection.

runs_as.definition: The identity the component runs under in the generated system: a service account. What the component may do on the platform is what the active rules say about the roles its principal holds; `oto policy iam` turns that into the platform's bindings, and the generated control on each resource safeguards the component too.

derives_from.definition: The rules a generated control was derived from: the permits that made its bindings and the forbids that withheld one. A control a person declared derives from nothing.

safeguards.definition: What the control applies to. The architecture's relation, widened to the data layer: a generated IAM control safeguards the table or the column the bindings are on.

effect.definition: Whether the rule grants the permission or refuses it. A forbid outranks every permit in Cedar's own semantics.

priority.definition: The order rules are listed in the bundle, highest first; it carries no meaning to Cedar, where forbid always wins, and it helps a reader find the rule that matters.

status.definition: A rule is a draft until a named person activates it (`oto decide <rule> status=active`), and retired when it no longer applies. Only an active rule compiles.

rationale.definition: Why the rule exists, in a sentence, carried into the bundle as a comment so the policy file explains itself.

action.definition: What the permission allows to be done.

resource_class.definition: The class of resource the permission is about, as the vocabulary names it: Table, Column, DataStore, Component or Interface.

selector.definition: Conditions over the resource's attributes that must all hold, each `key=value` or `key!=value` (`pii=false`, `classification!=restricted`); a value reads as true, false, a number or text. A boolean nobody set reads as false, so `pii=false` admits a table nobody marked; any other absent value is equal to nothing. Empty, the permission covers every resource of its class.

cloud_role.definition: The platform role that grants the action on the resource's kind, when the generated system's IAM is derived (`roles/bigquery.dataViewer` for a read on a table, `roles/bigquery.dataEditor` for a write). A fact of the permission, not a catalogue in the engine: the organisation says what its platform calls the right. A permission without one binds nothing, and the generator says so.

classification.definition: How the table's data is classified, as the organisation's scheme says it; a selector can read it.

pii.definition: Whether the table holds personal data. Derived true when one of its columns does; a person may also say so.

resource_uri.definition:
The table as the platform addresses it (`//bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/

/datasets//tables/`), when the generated system's IAM is derived; a table with none is bound to nothing, and the generator says so.

classification.definition: How the column's data is classified.

pii.definition: Whether the column holds personal data: a name, an address, an email, an identifier of a person.

kind.definition: A person's account, or a service account with no person behind it.

identity.definition: The account as the identity provider names it: an email, a service account name, a workload identity.
